persons.bio: Moses' elder brother and spokesman, made the first high priest of Israel. He also fashioned the golden calf while Moses was on Sinai.
Adam's second son, a keeper of sheep, whose offering God accepted and who was killed by his brother Cain — the first death recorded in Scripture.
Called out of Ur to a land he did not know, he received the covenant promise of descendants as numerous as the stars. Father of Isaac and Ishmael, and the ancestor through whom the promise passed.
The first man, formed from the dust and placed in Eden. Father of Cain, Abel, and Seth, through whom the line of Genesis 5 continues.
Taken captive to Babylon as a youth, he served under Nebuchadnezzar and successive kings while refusing to abandon his devotion, and received the visions recorded in his book.
The shepherd boy anointed by Samuel who became Israel's second king, united the kingdom, and made Jerusalem its capital. The royal line and the messianic promise both run through him.
A prophetess who judged Israel from beneath her palm tree and summoned Barak to battle against Sisera's army.
The prophet who confronted Ahab and the priests of Baal on Carmel, and was taken up in a whirlwind rather than dying.
Elijah's successor, who asked for a double portion of his spirit and served as prophet through the reigns of several kings of Israel.
A Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai who became queen of Persia and risked her life to expose Haman's plot against her people.
The first woman, formed as a companion for Adam and named "mother of all living." Mother of Cain, Abel, and Seth.
The son promised to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, bound on Mount Moriah and spared. Father of Esau and Jacob.
Prophet in Judah through four reigns, called in the year King Uzziah died, whose book contains the servant songs and the promise of Immanuel.
Isaac's younger son, who bought the birthright, wrestled at Peniel and was renamed Israel. His twelve sons became the tribes of the nation.

persons.disambiguator: son of Josiah, king of Judah

persons.bio: Called as a youth to prophesy against Judah before the exile, he saw Jerusalem fall and is traditionally credited with Lamentations.
Born in Bethlehem to Mary, of the line of David through both recorded genealogies. Crucified under Pontius Pilate and proclaimed risen by his followers.
A blameless man of Uz who lost his children, wealth, and health, and contended with God about it. His family appears nowhere else in Scripture.
A fisherman, son of Zebedee, called with his brother James. Traditionally identified with the disciple "whom Jesus loved."
Jacob's favoured son, sold into Egypt by his brothers, who rose to rule under Pharaoh and preserved his family through the famine.
A carpenter of Nazareth, betrothed to Mary. Matthew and Luke give him different fathers, and both trace his descent from David.
Moses' assistant and one of the two spies who trusted the promise. He led Israel across the Jordan and through the conquest of Canaan.
Jacob's fourth son, who proposed selling Joseph and later offered himself in Benjamin's place. The royal tribe descends from him.
A young woman of Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph, who bore Jesus. She appears again at Cana, at the cross, and among the disciples after the ascension.
King of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham and received a tithe. Hebrews notes he appears without recorded genealogy.
Sister of Moses and Aaron, who watched over him in the reeds and led Israel's women in song after the crossing of the sea.
A Jew of the exile in Susa who raised his cousin Esther, refused to bow to Haman, and was raised to high office in Persia.
Drawn from the Nile and raised in Pharaoh's household, he led Israel out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai, and died within sight of the promised land.

persons.primaryName: Mother of the Wife of Simon

persons.bio: King of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and carried Judah into exile. His dreams and their interpretations run through the book of Daniel.
Found righteous in a corrupt generation, he built the ark and survived the flood with his family. Father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
A Pharisee who persecuted the early church until his encounter on the Damascus road, after which he carried the message across the Roman world and wrote much of the New Testament.
A fisherman of Galilee called with his brother Andrew, who confessed Jesus as the Christ, denied him, and was restored.
Found at the well by Abraham's servant and married to Isaac. She secured the blessing for her younger son Jacob.
A Moabite widow who refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi, gleaned in the fields of Boaz, and became great-grandmother to David.
Given to the sanctuary as a child, he became the last judge and the prophet who anointed both Saul and David.
Abraham's wife, who laughed at the promise of a son and bore Isaac at ninety. She sent Hagar and Ishmael away.
Israel's first king, chosen from Benjamin, whose reign unravelled after he disobeyed Samuel. He died with his sons at Gilboa.
David's son by Bathsheba, who asked for wisdom, built the temple, and ruled at the height of Israel's power. His foreign wives turned his heart late in life.
